method: Flesch Kincaid grade plus five, using a vowel-group syllable heuristic. Punctuated sentences and standalone task lines are counted as sentence units. Exact corpora and hashes retained. Quantity table fragments, headings, staff text, dates, lesson codes and the verbatim scheme outcome are excluded. Estimates guide editing; they are not learner assessments. Read-aloud and confirmed scribing routes are available.

1 Measure each cut size and fold mark. Aim within 2 mm of the written size; use a difference to improve, not to grade.
2 Check the tab is inside the triangle and the U channel has its back flange taped to the lower front face, a shelf projecting out and an upward front stop.
3 Use one landscape 80 mm by 60 mm card. On a clear level desk, support it in the U channel for 30 seconds without a hand. Stop if the stand tips or the card slips.
4 Record what really happened, one change and why. A planned test is not a completed test.

Hands away for 30 seconds, then remove the one landscape 80 by 60 mm card by hand. No shaking, pushing, dropping, extra load or personal item. Stop if the stand tips or the card slips. For an approved PVA route, full cure must be complete before testing.
With no card, tools, paper or printer, hear the model material descriptions and written sizes. Point, speak or sign a material choice and reason. Rehearse the steps with empty hands. An adult records exact confirmed words when a recording method is available. Mark transcription pending until it exists. A card mock-up and material tests stay pending; rehearsal is not practical evidence.

An adult approves actual materials, hand tools and support before any practical. A plan or quiz does not authorise tool use.
1 Wait for the adult to approve the actual material, hand tool and work area. No power tools or heated tools.
2 The adult checks scissors are suitable for the actual card or board. If cutting is difficult, stop; use adult-prepared parts. Do not force the blades.
3 Cut seated or in the agreed stable position, on a clear surface. Keep fingers clear. Close scissors for pauses and carry them only as the adult has shown.
4 Use the agreed cold join. For PVA, the adult checks the actual label and materials. Follow the stated handling and full cure instructions. Do not guess a cure time.
5 Hot glue is a comparison only. Do not plug in or use a hot-glue tool. Dowel or wood cutting is not part of the default card route.
6 For any concern, stop, put tools down and tell the adult. Restart only when the adult has checked and cleared the concern.
Tools down. Compare with the written plan and measure. Ask the adult if unsure. Adjust one approved feature and recheck. Resume only when the adult clears the concern. Return tools and clear offcuts as directed.
No craft knives, blade scoring, saws or drills in the taught card method. Practical work not done stays pending.

Weekly outcome verbatim: CONSTRUCTION: select materials and plan the build.
I can choose a material and safe join, plan the parts and steps, and check a card mock-up.
[ ] I can link a material property to the stand purpose.
[ ] I can record sizes, tools and a safety step in my plan.
[ ] I can make a card mock-up and use it to improve the plan.
Invented client Sam needs one landscape paper prompt card to stay upright on a clear desk. The card is 80 mm wide and 60 mm high. The default body base is 120 mm by 80 mm. The whole stand, including the channel, should fit a clear table area 160 mm wide by 120 mm deep. Design a small tabletop stand that supports it for 30 seconds without a hand, is easy to move, and has no loose sharp parts. Do not use a phone, cable or personal item for the test.
Adult model: thin card for the Week 2 mock-up and paper tape for the cold join. Thin card is easy to fold. The triangular shape may hold the card upright. Test the actual mock-up. A final material change needs a revised plan and adult check before Week 3.
Body 120 by 260 mm, crosswise folds 80, 160 and 240 mm from the same short edge. U channel 100 by 30 mm, long folds 10 and 20 mm from the same long edge. Test card 80 by 60 mm.
A mock-up can show a useful change before the main build. Record the real result and keep your revised plan. A model description or imagined test is not practical evidence.
